Agent: Sir, this is Priya from Fintech Collections. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4521. Your EMI of 18,500 rupees was due on the 15th of this month, and it's now the 22nd. Can we discuss the payment status?

Customer: Haan, I know, I know. Mujhe pata hai. But listen, I've already paid once before and you people called me again. This is the third time this week someone is calling me. Kal bhi call aya tha, parso bhi call aya tha. It's too much, yaar.

Agent: I understand, sir. I apologize for the inconvenience. But we need to resolve this outstanding amount of 18,500 rupees. Can you tell me when you can make the payment?

Customer: See, the problem is not that I don't want to pay. I will pay, but not like this. You keep calling me at random times. Kal morning 8:30 baje call aya tha — 8:30! That's before office hours. And then evening ko 8 baje another call. This is harassment, Priya. Mujhe nahi pasand.

Agent: Sir, I sincerely apologize. That should not have happened. Let me note this down. But sir, regarding the payment, can we at least schedule a specific date when you can pay the full amount?

Customer: Haan, I can pay by the 25th, next Monday. But before that, I want to speak to someone senior. Ek manager se baat karna chahta hoon. Aur ek aur baat — I want everything in writing. No more calls. Sirf email se communicate karo. I don't trust verbal promises anymore because last time someone promised something and then nothing happened.

Agent: Sir, I understand your frustration. Let me escalate this to my supervisor. But can I confirm — you're committing to pay 18,500 rupees by Monday the 25th?

Customer: Haan, 25th ko payment kar dunga. But this is conditional — conditional on the fact that you people stop calling me every day. Aur mujhe manager se baat karni hai. Ek senior person se. Not you, not another junior agent. Someone who can actually take responsibility and ensure that no more calls come after I pay.

Agent: Understood, sir. I'm noting down your escalation request. You want to speak with a manager, you want written communication only, and you're committing to pay 18,500 by the 25th of this month. Is that correct?

Customer: Haan, bilkul. But I'm serious about this. Agar aur ek call aaya, to main RBI ko complaint kar dunga. Aur mera lawyer bhi hai jo yeh sab dekh raha hai. So please, escalate this properly. I don't want to take legal action, but if you keep harassing me like this, I will have no choice.

Agent: Sir, I completely understand. I'm escalating your case to our grievance cell and our senior management team right now. They will contact you within 24 hours with a manager who can discuss a formal resolution plan with you. No further calls will be made until that happens. Can I get your preferred contact number and email for the manager to reach you?

Customer: Email is rajesh.kumar.1985@gmail.com. And the number is the same one you're calling — 9876543210. But please, make sure it's a senior person. And send me a written confirmation of this escalation, okay? I want proof that this has been escalated.

Agent: Absolutely, sir. I'm sending you an email confirmation right now with your escalation ticket number — that's ESC-2024-78451. A senior manager will reach out within 24 hours. Your payment commitment of 18,500 rupees by the 25th is noted, and no further collection calls will be made until the manager contacts you. Thank you for your patience, sir.

Customer: Okay, thank you. But remember — written communication only from now on. Aur agar koi aur call aaye, to I'm filing a complaint. Samjha?

Agent: Completely understood, sir. Escalation ticket ESC-2024-78451. Manager contact within 24 hours. Written communication only. Thank you, sir. Have a good day.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya calling from Finserve Collections. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4521. Do you have a few minutes to speak with me?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know about this loan. But listen, I have a big problem with your company. I don't want to talk about payment right now.

Agent: Okay, I understand. What's the issue, Rajesh? I'm here to help.

Customer: The problem is with the credit bureau report. You people have reported my account incorrectly to CIBIL. My credit score has gone down because of this, and I'm very upset about it. I applied for a home loan last month and they rejected me because of this wrong reporting.

Agent: I see. Can you tell me more specifically what you believe is incorrect in the bureau reporting?

Customer: Yes, yes. You are showing that I have defaulted on this loan, but I have made payments. I made a payment of 15,000 rupees in July itself. But on CIBIL, it is still showing as overdue. The amount you are showing as outstanding is also wrong. You are saying I owe 87,000 rupees, but after my July payment, it should be much less than that.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh, I understand your concern. Let me clarify — we need to verify the payment you made in July. Can you provide me with the transaction reference or the date when you made that payment?

Customer: I made it through UPI, na. I don't remember the exact reference, but I definitely sent the money. And even if there is some small amount pending, why is the bureau report showing it as a default? This is affecting my credit score very badly. My wife is also very worried about this.

Agent: I completely understand your frustration, Rajesh. These bureau reports are very important. Before we discuss any payment, I need to escalate this to our verification team. They will check your payment records and also verify what has been reported to CIBIL. Can I take your email address so we can send you the findings?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, but I want to know — will you correct the bureau report? Because I will not make any payment until this is corrected. How can I pay when my credit is already damaged? First, you correct the report, then we can talk about payment.

Agent: That's a fair point, Rajesh. I can understand why you want the bureau report corrected first. However, I need to be honest with you — the bureau correction process takes time and requires verification from our side. What I can do is escalate your dispute to our senior team today itself. They will review your July payment, verify the outstanding amount, and if there is an error, we will file a correction request with CIBIL.

Customer: How long will this take? I need this done quickly. My home loan application is pending, and I need to show a corrected credit report.

Agent: The verification usually takes 5 to 7 working days, and if we find an error, the bureau correction can take another 10 to 15 days. But Rajesh, I want to ask you — even while we are verifying this, would you be open to making a partial payment towards the account? This can also help improve your credit profile while we sort out the bureau issue.

Customer: No, no. I don't want to make any payment until this is sorted. Why should I pay if the amount itself is wrong and the bureau report is wrong? First, you verify everything, correct the report, and then we can talk. I am not going to pay anything until this is resolved.

Agent: I hear you, Rajesh. Let me escalate this to our disputes team right now. I will create a ticket for bureau reporting verification. Can I confirm your email address and a contact number where we can reach you with updates?

Customer: My email is rajesh.kumar1985@gmail.com. And you can call me on this number itself. But please, make sure someone from your senior team calls me back within two days with an update. I don't want to keep calling you people.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh. I will mark this as urgent. You will receive a call from our disputes team within 48 hours with an update on your July payment verification and the bureau reporting issue. In the meantime, if you have any documentation of that July payment — like a bank statement or UPI receipt — please keep it ready. That will help speed up the verification.

Customer: Okay, I will look for it. But remember, no payment until this is corrected. I am very serious about this.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. I have noted your position. Your ticket number is DIS-2024-78945. Please keep this for your reference. We will be in touch within 48 hours.

Customer: Thank you. I hope you people sort this out quickly.

Agent: Thank you for your patience, Rajesh. We will do our best. Have a good day.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Zenith Finance. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4782. Your EMI of 18,500 rupees was due on the 15th of this month, and we haven't received payment yet. It's now the 22nd. Can we discuss this?

Customer: Look, I know about the EMI. I've been meaning to call you people. The thing is, I'm having some issues right now. My business has been slow, and I'm trying to manage multiple loans at the same time. It's not easy.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. We want to help you. Can you tell me when you might be able to make this payment? Even a partial payment would help us move forward.

Customer: I don't know exactly when. Maybe next week, maybe the week after. I'm waiting for some money to come in from a client. But honestly, I'm getting frustrated with all these calls. This is the third call in two days.

Agent: I apologize for the frequency, Rajesh. We're just trying to resolve this. Your current outstanding balance is 1,23,450 rupees. If you can commit to a payment date, we can reduce the call frequency. What works for you?

Customer: <interruption> Wait, wait. 1,23,450? That doesn't sound right. I calculated it myself last week, and it should be around 95,000. You're charging me extra interest or something. I want to know exactly what's in that amount.

Agent: Let me explain, Rajesh. The 1,23,450 includes your principal outstanding, accrued interest, and a late fee that was applied after the due date passed. I can send you a detailed statement if you'd like to verify.

Customer: This is exactly what I'm talking about. You people just keep adding charges without explaining anything properly. And now you're calling me repeatedly like I'm some kind of criminal. I've been a customer for three years. I've paid most of my EMIs on time.

Agent: You're right, Rajesh, and I apologize. Let's focus on getting this resolved. Would you be open to a settlement discussion, or can you commit to paying the full amount by a specific date?

Customer: Settlement? No, no. I'm not interested in any settlement right now. And frankly, I'm done with these calls. I've decided to take legal action against your company. I'm consulting with my lawyer tomorrow, and he's going to handle all communication from now on. You should not be calling me directly anymore. All future contact should go through my legal representative.

Agent: Rajesh, I understand you're frustrated, but let's not escalate this. We can work out a payment plan that suits your situation. There's no need for legal involvement at this stage.

Customer: No, you don't understand. I've been researching my rights, and I believe your company has violated several RBI guidelines on collection practices. The excessive calls, the unexplained charges — all of this is documented. My lawyer will be sending you a formal notice within the next 48 hours. Until then, do not call this number again. Is that clear?

Agent: Yes, Rajesh, I hear you. I will make a note of this on your account. Can I at least get your lawyer's contact details so we can coordinate directly with them?

Customer: You'll receive the notice with all the details. That's all you need. And if you or anyone from your company calls me again before my lawyer contacts you, I will be filing a formal complaint with the RBI as well. I'm not bluffing. Goodbye.

Agent: Rajesh, wait—

Customer: <interruption> I said goodbye. Don't call again.

Agent: Sir, a settlement means we're waiving off the accumulated penalties and some interest. Normally, at this stage of delinquency, we would be looking at the full outstanding amount. This is a significant concession.

Customer: I hear what you're saying, but honestly, I cannot commit to that figure right now. I need to discuss this with my wife. We paid Rs. 1,50,000 as per that settlement, and the agent at that time told us the account would be cleared. But then after a few months, you people started calling again saying there was still an outstanding balance. So I'm hesitant to agree to another settlement without seeing something in writing first.

Agent: <interruption> I completely understand your frustration, sir. Let me clarify — was that previous settlement fully honoured? Did you receive a closure letter or NOC at that time?

Customer: No, we didn't receive any closure letter. That's exactly the problem. The agent said the account would be settled, we made the payment, and then silence for a few months. Then suddenly the calls started again. So how can I trust that this settlement will actually close the account?

Customer: No, no, you're not listening to me. I made a payment. The payment was successful. I have the UPI reference number. So the bureau should show my account as current, not 90 days overdue. Agent: I understand your frustration, Rajesh. Let me check the payment records. <pause> I see a payment of Rs. 50,000 was received on the 15th of last month. Is that the payment you're referring to?

Customer: Haan, yes, I know about the account. What is it? I have been meaning to call you people actually.

Customer: See, Priya, I want to pay, I really do. But the situation is... it's very difficult right now. We had the floods, na? The monsoon floods in Kerala last month completely destroyed my warehouse. My entire business stock — textiles, fabrics, everything — it's all gone. The water came so fast, we couldn't even move anything out.

Agent: Oh, I'm very sorry to hear that, Rajesh. That must be extremely stressful. Can you tell me a bit more about the impact on your business? Are you still able to operate?

Customer: <interruption> No, no, the warehouse is completely damaged. The building itself — the walls, the roof — everything needs repair. And the stock, Priya, the stock was worth almost 8 lakhs. I have lost everything. Right now I am trying to get insurance claims processed, but you know how slow that is. The surveyor came last week, but the claim will take at least two to three months to settle.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. This is clearly a major external disruption to your business. Have you been able to generate any income since the floods, or is the business completely halted?

Customer: Completely halted. I cannot operate from that location anymore. I am looking for an alternative warehouse space, but that also requires capital which I don't have right now. My wife is very worried. We have been living off our savings, but that is also running out. I have not paid my own house rent for the last month because of this situation.

Agent: Rajesh, I can hear the stress in your voice, and I want to help you find a solution. Before we discuss options, let me ask — do you have any timeline on when the insurance claim might come through? Or any other source of funds that might help in the near term?

Customer: The insurance company said maybe two to three months, but honestly, I don't trust their timeline. They are very slow. As for other funds... my brother-in-law offered to help, but he is also facing some financial pressure right now. I am hoping to restart operations in a smaller space within the next month or so, but I need capital for that.

Agent: Okay, so you are looking at a one to three month window before you can stabilize your cash flow again. Is that fair to say?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. One month minimum, maybe two or three months to get back to normal operations and start generating income again.

Agent: Rajesh, given this situation, I want to explore some options with you. One option is to request a moratorium — a temporary pause on your EMI payments for two to three months while you recover. This would give you breathing room. However, I need to escalate this to my supervisor for approval. Can you provide me with some documentation of the flood damage? Photos, insurance claim reference, anything that supports what you are telling me?

Customer: Yes, yes, I have photos on my phone. I also have the insurance claim form that I filed. I can send these to you. But Priya, will this moratorium affect my credit score? I am already worried about that.

Agent: That is a valid concern, Rajesh. It is much better than letting the account slip further into arrears. I will need to send you a formal request form to fill out, and you will need to attach the documentation.

Customer: Okay, okay. How long will the approval take?

Agent: Usually three to five business days once we receive the complete documentation. In the meantime, can you commit to making a partial payment towards the current outstanding amount? Even Rs. 50,000 would help reduce the pressure on the account.

Customer: Let me think... maybe by next week I can arrange Rs. 10,000. My wife's jewelry — she is willing to sell some of it if needed. But I cannot promise more than that right now.

Agent: That is very helpful, Rajesh. So you are committing to Rs. 10,000 by next week, and you will submit the moratorium request with documentation by then as well. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, yes. I will send the photos and the insurance claim form by tomorrow itself. And I will try to arrange the 10,000 by next Friday.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Namaste Rajesh, this is Priya from Fintech Solutions Collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4782. Do you have a few minutes to speak with me?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know about the loan. What is it? I am a bit busy right now.

Agent: I understand. This will just take five minutes. Rajesh, your account is currently 45 days overdue. Your last EMI of 18,500 rupees was due on the 15th of this month, and we have not received payment yet. Can you tell me what is happening?

Customer: See, I know I am late. But the thing is, my business has been very slow these past two months. The construction project I was working on got delayed, so my income has become very irregular. I cannot pay the full 18,500 right now.

Agent: I see. So you are facing some income disruption at the moment. How much can you pay today, Rajesh?

Customer: Today I cannot pay anything. But listen, I want to talk to you about something else. This EMI of 18,500 is too much for me now. When I took the loan, my business was doing well, but now... <interruption> sorry, my wife is calling me. One moment.

Agent: No problem, take your time.

Customer: Okay, I am back. So what I am thinking is, can you reduce my EMI? Maybe to 12,000 or 13,000 per month? And maybe extend the loan tenure? I still want to repay, but I need some breathing room. The current structure is killing me.

Agent: That is a very reasonable request, Rajesh. I appreciate that you are being proactive about this. Let me understand your situation better. You are saying your monthly income has reduced due to the project delay, correct?

Customer: Yes, exactly. Before, I was making around 60,000 to 70,000 per month from the construction work. Now it is maybe 30,000 to 35,000. And I have other expenses too — my daughter's school fees, my mother's medical bills. So the 18,500 EMI is just... it is not possible right now.

Agent: I completely understand, Rajesh. What you are asking for — an EMI reduction and tenure extension — these are restructuring options that we do offer to customers in genuine hardship. However, I cannot approve this on the call myself. This needs to go to our Loan Restructuring Committee for assessment.

Customer: Okay, so what do I need to do? How long will this take?

Agent: Here is what will happen. I will create a formal request for restructuring based on what you have told me today. You will need to provide some supporting documents — your last three months of bank statements to show your current income, and ideally a letter from your employer or client confirming the project delay. Do you have these documents?

Customer: Bank statements, yes, I can get those. But a letter from my client... that might be difficult. They are not very formal people. Can I just show my bank statements?

Agent: Bank statements are the most important. If you can get a letter, that strengthens your case, but we can work with statements alone. Now, while we process your restructuring request, what about the overdue amount of 45 days? Can you make a partial payment towards that?

Customer: How much are you asking for?

Agent: If you can pay 8,000 to 10,000 towards the overdue amount, that would show good faith and buy us some time while the restructuring is being reviewed. Can you do that within the next week?

Customer: <interruption> Let me think... I have some money coming in from a small project next week. If that comes through, I can pay 8,000. But I cannot promise more than that right now.

Agent: That is fair, Rajesh. So you are committing to pay 8,000 towards the overdue amount within the next week, pending the money coming in. And you will send me your bank statements by when?

Customer: I can send them by Friday. This Friday, okay?

Agent: Perfect. Friday is good. Now, let me take down your email address so I can send you the restructuring request form. What is your email?

Customer: It is rajesh.kumar1982@gmail.com. And my phone number is still the same, right?

Agent: Yes, we have 9876543210 on file. Is that still correct?

Customer: Yes, that is correct.

Agent: Excellent. So to summarize: you will send your bank statements by Friday to support your restructuring request. You are committing to pay 8,000 towards the overdue amount within the next week. We will process your request for EMI reduction and tenure extension, and someone from our restructuring team will contact you within 5 to 7 business days with an update. Does that sound good?

Customer: Yes, that sounds good. But I want to make sure — if the restructuring is approved, the new EMI will be lower, right? And the tenure will be extended?

Agent: That is the intent, yes. The committee will review your income situation and propose a new structure that is manageable for you. There is no guarantee on the exact numbers until they review, but based on what you have shared, there is a good case for both EMI reduction and tenure extension.

Customer: Okay, I trust you. I will send the documents on Friday. And I will try to pay the 8,000 next week.

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. I really appreciate your cooperation and honesty about your situation. We will be in touch very soon. Take care.

Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar? This is Priya calling from Finserve Collections regarding your loan account.

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh. But... but I am not in a good state right now. My wife, she is not well. She is in the hospital since yesterday and I... I don't know what to do.

Agent: I understand, sir. I hope she recovers soon. I am calling regarding your EMI payment which was due on the 15th of this month. Your account shows an outstanding balance of Rs. 47,500 against your personal loan of Rs. 2,50,000. Can we discuss the payment?

Customer: Payment? How can I think about payment when my wife is lying in the hospital? The doctors say she needs more tests, more medicines. I have spent everything on her treatment already. I... I don't even know if I can afford the next round of medicines.

Agent: Sir, I completely understand this is a difficult time. But we need to address this outstanding amount. The EMI was due on the 15th. Today is the 22nd, so you are already seven days overdue. Can you commit to paying by the end of this week?

Customer: End of this week? How? I have no money left. My salary comes on the 5th of next month, but even that... even that will go to the hospital bills. I am so confused right now. I cannot think clearly. Everything is happening so fast. My head is spinning.

Agent: Sir, I hear you. Let me ask — do you have any family member who can help you with this payment? A relative, a friend, anyone?

Customer: No, no one. My parents are old, they cannot help. My brother is in Dubai but he has his own problems. I am alone in this. I am completely alone. Sometimes I think... I think I cannot handle all this. The loan, the hospital, the bills, everything. It is too much. Too much for one person.

Agent: Sir, I want to help you find a solution. But I need to understand your situation better. Are you saying you cannot make any payment right now, or can you manage a partial payment of, say, Rs. 15,000 this week?

Customer: Partial? I don't have Rs. 15,000. I don't have Rs. 5,000. I have maybe Rs. 2,000 in my account and that is for food and transport. My wife's hospital bill is Rs. 35,000 already and they are asking for more. I... I am not thinking straight. I feel like everything is falling apart. I don't know what I am saying anymore.

Agent: Sir, I can hear that you are under a lot of stress. This is a medical emergency situation. Let me note this down as a hardship case due to medical emergency. I am going to escalate your account to our senior team who can discuss restructuring options with you — maybe extending your loan tenure or reducing your EMI temporarily.

Customer: Restructuring? Will that help? I don't know. I don't even know if I will be able to pay anything next month. My wife... she might need surgery. The doctors are still deciding. I am so scared. I cannot focus on anything else right now.

Agent: Sir, I understand. What I am going to do is flag your account as requiring specialist handling. You will be contacted by our senior collections officer within 24 hours, and they will discuss options that are suitable for your situation. In the meantime, please focus on your wife's health. Can you confirm your current contact number is still 9876543210?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. But please... please tell your senior officer to be gentle with me. I am not trying to avoid the loan. I just... I just cannot handle this right now. I am breaking down. I am sorry.

Agent: Sir, there is no need to apologize. You are going through a very difficult time. I am marking your account as requiring empathy-based handling due to the medical emergency and the emotional distress you are experiencing. Our specialist team will contact you soon. Take care of yourself and your wife.

Customer: Thank you. Thank you for understanding. I... I hope things get better. I hope my wife gets well soon.

Agent: We hope so too, sir. Goodbye, and please take care.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. Who is this?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya calling from Credible Finance. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4521. You have an outstanding balance of Rs 47,300 and your EMI of Rs 8,500 was due on the 15th of this month. Can we discuss your payment status?

Customer: Look, I've already told your people about this. You guys have called me four times in the last two days. Four times, Priya. I'm getting calls at 6:30 in the morning, at 8 PM in the evening. This is harassment. I have a job, I have a family, and I cannot be disturbed like this.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh, and I apologize if the frequency has been high. But we do need to resolve this outstanding amount. Can you tell me when you'll be able to make the payment?

Customer: That's not the point. The point is your company is calling me outside business hours. I checked the RBI guidelines — you're not supposed to call before 9 AM or after 7 PM. And you're calling my office number too. My boss asked me why a collection agency is calling me at work. Do you understand how embarrassing that is?

Agent: I sincerely apologize for that, Rajesh. I can note that concern. But regarding the EMI itself, can we work out a payment plan? Are you facing any difficulty with the amount?

Customer: No, I'm not facing difficulty. I can pay. But I'm not going to commit to anything until this calling harassment stops. You people are violating my privacy and my rights. I'm going to file a complaint with the RBI and also post about this on Twitter. Your company needs to know that this is not acceptable.

Agent: Rajesh, I understand your frustration. Let me escalate this to my supervisor right away. Can I at least confirm your current address so we can update our records and ensure no further calls go to your office?

Customer: My address is still the same — 42 Maple Gardens, Sector 5, Bangalore. But I'm serious about the complaint. I want written confirmation that you will stop calling me outside 9 AM to 7 PM, and that you will not contact my employer again. Until I get that in writing, I'm not making any payment commitment.

Agent: I completely understand, Rajesh. I'm going to escalate this immediately to our compliance team. They will review the call logs and ensure this doesn't happen again. You should expect contact from them within 24 hours with a formal acknowledgement. In the meantime, I'm noting your complaint on your account.

Customer: And I want to know who authorized calling my office. I want names. This is a serious breach of my privacy. I'm documenting everything and I will be filing a formal complaint with the RBI banking ombudsman. Make sure that's noted.

Agent: It's all being noted right now, Rajesh. Your complaint about excessive call frequency, calls outside permitted hours, and third-party contact at your workplace without your consent is being logged. I'm escalating this to our compliance and grievance cell immediately. You will hear from them within one business day. Is there anything else I should note?

Customer: Just make sure this is taken seriously. I shouldn't have to threaten legal action to get basic respect. And I expect a written response, not another phone call.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh. I'm marking this as urgent escalation to compliance. You'll receive written communication. Thank you for bringing this to our attention, and again, I apologize for the experience you've had.

Customer: Fine. Goodbye.

Agent: Goodbye, Rajesh.
